Phrase join key: fold, apostrophes closed, punctuation demoted to separator

Source: R/normalize.R
phrase_key.Rd

[normalize_string()] is a FOLD, not a key: it keeps punctuation, so `"ST. MARY"` and `"MARY-JO"` survive intact. [name_key()] keeps punctuation too, and additionally drops parenthesised alternate names. [compact_name_key()] deletes every non-letter, gluing word boundaries back together (`"VAN DER BERG"` -> `"VANDERBERG"`). None of the three is the contract a phrase-equality join needs: upper-case ASCII words separated by single spaces, punctuation demoted to a separator rather than kept or deleted.

Usage

phrase_key(x, remove_apostrophes = TRUE)

Arguments

x

character vector of phrases as recorded.

remove_apostrophes

logical: delete apostrophes before the punctuation pass (the join-key-safe default). `FALSE` lets the punctuation pass space them, splitting `"O'BRIEN"` into `"O BRIEN"`.

Value

character vector of `A-Z0-9` words separated by single spaces, `NA` where nothing keyable survives.

Details

Apostrophes are DELETED before the punctuation pass, not spaced. Spacing them splits one token into two, so `"O'BRIEN"` and `"OBRIEN"` – one surname recorded two ways – key as `"O BRIEN"` and `"OBRIEN"` and count as a disagreement. The fold maps the curly, modifier and okina forms onto the straight apostrophe before the delete runs, so all four codepoints close the token. Pass `remove_apostrophes = FALSE` only when the split is genuinely wanted; for a join key it never is.

Parenthesised text is NOT stripped – unlike [name_key()], every bracket is data here, because this key serves phrases (cities, organisations, addresses) where `"Michigan Otolaryngology (MOSA)"` is one value, not a name carrying an alternate. For person names under the alternate-name convention, use [name_key()] instead.

`NA` in, `NA` out; a phrase with no keyable characters is `NA`, never `""`, so absence cannot join to absence.

Examples

phrase_key(c("O'Brien", "OBrien", "St. Mary", "VAN  DER BERG", ""))
#> [1] "OBRIEN"       "OBRIEN"       "ST MARY"      "VAN DER BERG" NA            
# "OBRIEN" "OBRIEN" "ST MARY" "VAN DER BERG" NA
